reaction.episode: CORRECTION episode, data through Nov 23 (not stale): SPX 7,237.17, -7.74% from its 120-day high, -4.99% below its 50-day and -1.54% below its 200-day; SMH $460.18 and NVDA $165.05 both BELOW Zone 2 after Monday's sharp bounce (+15.03% / +31.48%); VIX 26.62, rolling over from a 35.89 five-day high; HY OAS 3.63 and calm; mechanical tally 3 of 4. The midday tape is already testing the bounce: NVDA $152.94 live, QQQ -2.03%.
reaction.invalidation: SPX reclaims 7,300 on a weekly close with NVDA holding above $175 (Zone 2) and VIX closing under 25 voids the Watch stance — the correction is over and the posture moves to Add. Conversely, HY OAS above 4.00% with SPX below 7,000 voids it the other way — the stance becomes staged Trim, not Watch.

reaction.trapRisk: Monday's bounce was news-driven (Huang's reinstatement: NVDA +31.48%, SMH +15.03% in a day) and is already giving back a large part of the move by midday Tuesday — the classic pivot-and-fail shape. No entry chases the first bounce: either the bounce holds above Monday's closes and reclaims Zone 2, or a second low forms and holds with the 10-year falling. Until one of those prints, every up day inside the correction is a trap candidate, not a buy signal.

strategyPosture: Watch. Monday's bounce is fading at midday, both SMH and NVDA sit below Zone 2, and the VIX at 26.29 is still above the 25 stand-down line — no tranche is armed and no probe is justified until a Zone 2 close or a second low that holds.

themes.counterRead: Index-level calm masks real weakness concentrated in the handful of names that dominate the index by weight — but the credit and breadth data say rotation, not systemic break. The risk is treating a Mag7 unwind as a market-wide sell signal and selling the parts of the book that are actually holding. Watch the gap: if lending standards tighten or HY OAS pushes toward 4.00%, the rotation read dies.
themes.dataAnchor: Mag7 names average 20.31% below their 52-week highs versus SPY only 8.2% below its high — a 12.11-point divergence gap. The weakest leader, NVDA, is 37.2% off its high while the strongest, AAPL, is just 2.4% off. Bank lending standards are LOOSE (SLOOS 1.7%, far below the ~40% stress threshold), HY OAS is 3.63 and calm, and IWM is up 0.64% today while QQQ falls 2.03%. Credit is not confirming an equity rollover.
themes.label: Rotation, not rollover — the unwind is concentrated in the leaders
themes.narrative: The tape reads like a broad market break: the Mag7 complex is deep off its highs and QQQ is down 10.45% in a month. The fear narrative says index leadership is collapsing into a general rollover.
themes.watchFor: HY OAS closing above 4.00% or SLOOS turning up — either flips this from rotation to rollover.

themes.counterRead: The fundamentals-versus-price gap is the widest in the book, which is exactly the setup — but a gap is not a bottom. Zone occupancy is the gate: neither name has printed a Zone 2 close, and the mechanical tally's zone-occupancy leg is unconfirmed. Buying the bounce before a Zone 2 print is paying for a story that Monday already repriced.
themes.dataAnchor: By midday Tuesday the bounce is giving back hard: NVDA live at $152.94, down 7.02% on the day, and SMH and NVDA both still sit BELOW Zone 2 (SMH Zone 2 is $470–505, NVDA Zone 2 is $175–185). Both are still ~32% below their 120-day highs (NVDA -32.18%, SMH -31.5%). Against that price action, fundamentals have not broken: NVDA revenue is growing 61.4% YoY, AVGO 55%, LRCX 131.3%, ONTO 41.5% — and the conviction screen ranks ONTO 85, AVGO 83, DDOG 82, AMAT 80.
themes.label: AI semis: Monday's violent bounce is already fading
themes.narrative: Huang's reinstatement was supposed to end the Nvidia crisis: NVDA jumped 31.48% Monday to $165.05 and SMH rose 15.03% to $460.18. The story says the leadership question is answered and the complex is healing.
themes.watchFor: SMH or NVDA closes inside Zone 2 (SMH $470–505, NVDA $175–185) — until then the bounce is unconfirmed.

themes.counterRead: This is a multiple-compression episode inside a structural theme, not a demand break — but VST's flat revenue inflection is the honest caveat: the power trade splits between names still growing into the story and names whose price ran ahead of their own numbers. Rank inside the theme, don't buy the theme.
themes.dataAnchor: The complex has given back a third to a half of its peak: VST is 34.1% off its high at $120.38 (-15.27% in a month), VRT is 54.3% off its high (-13.51% in a month), GEV is down 16.29% in a month, CCJ 24.17%, OKLO 24.9%, SMR 35.39%. Yet the operating data has not followed price down: VRT revenue is growing 27.7% YoY (conviction 79), BWXT revenue is up 18.3% YoY (conviction 77), and VST insiders bought $0.9M at the trough. VST's own revenue inflection reads STABLE_OR_DECLINING, so the theme is not uniform — the equipment and fuel names carry the growth, the merchant generator does not.
themes.label: Nuclear / AI power: the demand story survives, the multiple does not
themes.narrative: The AI-power trade was the cleanest second derivative of the buildout — Vistra, Vertiv, GE Vernova, the uranium names. The narrative said power demand was structural and repriced the whole complex upward.
themes.watchFor: VRT or BWXT holding their trough with revenue growth intact while VST's revenue inflection turns — divergence inside the theme decides the entries.

themes.counterRead: Leverage cuts both ways and this is the proof — the sleeve that amplified the upside is now amplifying a 60% drawdown with no fundamental floor to catch it. The BMNR audit's condition (add only if ETH reclaims $1,800 and holds) is nowhere near met. Nothing in this tape argues for averaging down; the only question is whether the position sizes still match a sleeve with no anchor.
themes.dataAnchor: The one-month tape is a wipeout: CONL is down 60.96% in a month and 10.45% today alone, BMNR is down 36.83% in a month and 8.22% today, BTC is down 22.61%, ETH 26.15%, DOGE 26.57%, IBIT 25.1%, COIN 35.18%. CONL, BMNR and DOGE are all holdings, so this is not a watchlist problem — it is live P&L. The input carries no revenue or cash-flow anchor for any crypto name: the sleeve is pure multiple and sentiment, which is why it falls fastest when sentiment turns.
themes.label: Crypto leverage: the book's leveraged sleeve is the bleeding edge
themes.narrative: The leveraged crypto sleeve was the portfolio's upside engine — CONL and BMNR as geared exposure to BTC and ETH, DOGE as the momentum tail. The narrative said leverage was the way to hold crypto through the cycle.
themes.watchFor: ETH reclaiming $1,800 and holding — the standing BMNR add condition — or CONL stabilizing above its November lows before any sizing conversation.

themes.counterRead: Aligned does not mean safe. The permission is intact only while credit stays calm — HY OAS widening toward 4.00% would change the regime faster than any equity level. Rates are the tripwire, not the trigger: watch the spread, not the 10-year yield.
themes.dataAnchor: The curve says otherwise: 2Y 4.63%, 10Y 4.92%, 30Y 5.31% with a positive 2s10s slope of +0.29, real 10Y at 2.79%, breakeven inflation 2.13%, and HY OAS at 3.63 — calm and 37bp below the 4.00% stand-down line. The Fed funds rate is 3.88%. Nothing in the rates complex is screaming stress; the correction is an equity repricing, not a credit event. The calendar agrees: PCE Oct prints Nov 25 and the FOMC decides Dec 8–9, and both are priced as the next information, not the next crisis.
themes.label: Rates and credit: the macro permission for risk is intact
themes.narrative: With equities correcting and the 10-year near 5%, the story says rates are the problem — tight money choking the AI buildout and forcing the unwind.
themes.watchFor: HY OAS closing above 4.00% or the Nov 25 PCE print shifting Dec-hike odds into the Dec 8–9 FOMC.

watchFor: SMH or NVDA closes inside Zone 2 (SMH $470–505, NVDA $175–185) — arms Tranche A only with the tally at 3/6 or better.
PCE Oct print Nov 25 and Dec-hike odds into the Dec 8–9 FOMC.
HY OAS closes above 4.00% or VIX closes above 35 (5-day high 35.89) — regime-break confirmation.
SPX weekly close below 7,000 (a second week) versus a reclaim of 7,300.
NVDA holds above $150 and SMH above its Monday close of $460.18 — if either fails, the bounce is a trap.
whereWaveBuilds: The next move builds around the Nov 25 PCE print and the Dec 8–9 FOMC decision: either soft inflation data drives a Zone 2 reclaim in SMH/NVDA, or the failed bounce retests Monday's lows and forces the second-low question.
